subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): import legacy auth-profiles.json into SQLite store on load

question: Should OpenClaw allow normal auth-profile runtime loads to import and persist legacy `auth-profiles.json`, or must this recovery stay in doctor/startup migration code?
rationale: The PR solves a real upgrade failure but changes where secret-bearing legacy credential data is trusted and persisted, so automation should not pick that product/security boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Keep Runtime SQLite-Only
options.body: Move recovery into doctor or a maintainer-approved startup/update migration boundary and keep normal auth reads from consuming legacy JSON.

options.title: Approve Runtime Fallback
options.body: Accept the compatibility fallback only with updated invariant tests, docs, and security expectations around retired credential JSON.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: If runtime fallback is not desired, pause or close this PR while the canonical issue is solved through a narrower migration or warning path.

recommendation.title: Keep Runtime SQLite-Only
recommendation.body: Move recovery into doctor or a maintainer-approved startup/update migration boundary and keep normal auth reads from consuming legacy JSON.

likelyOwner.reason: The SQLite auth-store migration and current runtime/doctor boundary history point most directly to this owner for the product/security decision.
